# Grid header drag-and-drop scrambles grouped leaves on cross-group/region drops and traps ungrouped columns behind groups

## Context

During the Engine 13.4 release-gate verification matrix on `#20379` (*Grid columns can sit under a shared group header*, merged via `#20397` + `#20502`, evaluated on `dev` at `ccb30d8d6e`), real-pointer Playwright + Neural Link testing on `examples/grid/headerGroups` surfaced three defects in `Neo.draggable.grid.header.toolbar.SortZone` and `Neo.draggable.container.SortZone` covering Matrix Rows 2 and 4.

## The Problem

Measured in Chromium on `examples/grid/headerGroups` (`dev` at `ccb30d8d6e`):

1. **Row 2A & Row 4B — Dragging a non-boundary grouped leaf into another group or region scrambles its own group order instead of refusing the drop:**
   - `test/playwright/e2e/grid/HeaderGroups.spec.mjs:139-141, 177` only tested leaves that were *already* sitting at the boundary edge of their group (`Mar` at index `2` dragged right into `Q2`, `Apr` at index `3` dragged left into `Q1`, and `Jan` at index `0` dragged left onto `Region`).
   - When dragging **`Jan`** (index `0` of `Q1: ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar']`) rightward and releasing over **`May`** (in `Q2`), `SortZone` swaps `Jan` past `Feb` and `Mar` (`0 → 1 → 2`), refuses only the `2 → 3` boundary crossing, and commits `currentIndex = 2` on drop — mutating `Q1` to **`['Feb', 'Mar', 'Jan']`** (`ROW_2A_JAN_TO_MAY_ORDER: ["Feb","Mar","Jan","Apr","May","Jun"]`) even though the user dropped on `Q2`.
   - Likewise, when dragging **`Mar`** (index `2` of `Q1`) leftward and releasing over **`Region`** (`locked: 'start'`), `Mar` stays in `center` (`SortZone.mjs:419-420`), **but `Q1` is mutated to `['Mar', 'Jan', 'Feb']`** (`ROW_4A_MAR_TO_REGION: {"start":["Region"],"center":["Mar","Jan","Feb","Apr","May","Jun"]}`).
2. **Row 2B — An ungrouped column is permanently trapped behind a group in the same region:**
   - When dragging ungrouped **`Id`** (index `12`, after `Q4`) leftward to place it before `Q4` (`Oct`) in `center`, `container/SortZone#onDragMove` only steps `currentIndex` by `±1` (`12 → 11`, which is `Dec` in `Q4`). Because `switchItems(12, 11)` checks `getHeaderGroupId(12) !== getHeaderGroupId(11)` (`null !== Q4`), it refuses the swap and resets `currentIndex = 12` (`ROW_2B_ID_PAST_Q4_ORDER` remains `[...,"Oct","Nov","Dec","Id"]`). An ungrouped column can never be reordered past a group within the same region.
3. **Row 4C — Overdrag loop at internal group boundaries (`src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs:799-861`):**
   - When a grouped leaf at an internal group boundary (`Apr` at `index 3` dragged left past `localBoundary.left`, or `Mar` at `index 2` dragged right past `localBoundary.right` when the centre toolbar overflows) enters `isOverDraggingStart` / `isOverDraggingEnd`, `onDragMove` decrements/increments `me.currentIndex`, awaits `me.scrollToIndex()`, and calls `me.switchItems(index, me.currentIndex)`, which resets `me.currentIndex = index`. Because `me.currentIndex !== 0 && me.currentIndex !== maxItems` (`line 853`), `me.isOverDragging` stays `true` and re-schedules `onDragMove` every `30ms`.

## The Architectural Reality

- `Neo.draggable.grid.header.toolbar.SortZone#switchItems(index1, index2)` (`src/draggable/grid/header/toolbar/SortZone.mjs:561-567`) guards individual adjacent swaps (`if (me.getHeaderGroupId(index1) !== me.getHeaderGroupId(index2)) { me.currentIndex = index1; return }`), while `Neo.draggable.container.SortZone#onDragMove` (`src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs:827-839`) advances `currentIndex` one neighbour at a time (`index ± 1`).
- Because swaps inside the dragged leaf's own group succeed while the pointer moves toward another group or another region, `me.indexMap` and `me.itemRects` are already mutated by the time the pointer leaves the group. Simply clamping `currentIndex` at the group boundary leaves the leaf at the boundary edge instead of either restoring `me.startIndex` on an invalid cross-group/cross-region drop or keeping the leaf constrained cleanly.
- For an ungrouped column (`getHeaderGroupId(index1) === null`) crossing an adjacent group (`getHeaderGroupId(index2) !== null`), the atomic unit in the leaf toolbar is the entire contiguous run of `index2`'s `headerGroup.id` — an ungrouped column cannot land *inside* the group, but once the pointer crosses past the group's span, it must shift the contiguous group run as a block rather than halting at the first leaf of the group.

Design authority: `#20379` (*Grid columns can sit under a shared group header*) + 13.4 release-gate verification matrix (Rows 2 & 4).

## The Fix

1. **Preserve within-group order when a grouped leaf is released outside its group or over another region (Rows 2A & 4B):**
   - If a grouped leaf is released over a different group or a different region (`lastDragClientX` outside its group / over another region), or if within-group clamping is used, ensure that releasing a non-boundary leaf (e.g. `Jan` dropped on `May`, or `Mar` dropped on `Region`) does not silently commit an unintended reorder of its own group (restore `startIndex` when released outside the group's valid drop zone, or only reorder while the pointer is within the group's horizontal bounds).
2. **Allow ungrouped columns to reorder past a group in the same region (Row 2B):**
   - When an ungrouped leaf (`getHeaderGroupId(index1) === null`) is dragged across a group (`getHeaderGroupId(index2) !== null`), allow it to step across the entire contiguous group run (`[groupStart..groupEnd]`) as a unit once the pointer crosses the group's threshold, so `Id` dragged before `Q4` lands at `[..., 'Id', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec']` without splitting `Q4`.
3. **Prevent `isOverDragging` infinite retry when `switchItems` refuses a boundary step (Row 4C):**
   - In `src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs:799-861`, if `switchItems` refused the step (`me.currentIndex === index`), do not keep `me.isOverDragging = true` spinning when no further swap in that direction is possible.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1 (Row 2A & Row 4B — Non-boundary grouped leaf drop):** Dragging `Jan` (first leaf of `Q1`) onto `May` (`Q2`) and dragging `Mar` (last leaf of `Q1`) onto `Region` (`locked: 'start'`) both leave `Q1` in its original order `['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar']` (e2e).
- [ ] **AC-2 (Row 2B — Ungrouped column across a group):** Dragging ungrouped `Id` leftward past `Q4` (`Oct, Nov, Dec`) places `Id` immediately before `Oct` while keeping `Q4` contiguous (`['Id', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec']`) and `Q4`'s group cell aligned with `Oct..Dec` (e2e).
- [ ] **AC-3 (Row 4C — Overdrag boundary termination):** Overdragging a grouped boundary leaf (`Apr` or `Mar`) past the toolbar edge does not stick `isOverDragging` in a loop when `switchItems` refuses the swap.

## Out of Scope

- **Group-cell drag (`.neo-grid-header-group-cell` in `GroupRow`, Matrix Row 3):** `#20379` explicitly scoped out dragging a whole group header cell; with clean leaf reorder + ungrouped-across-group stepping (`AC-1`..`AC-3`), group-cell drag is deferred to a post-13.4 feature leaf unless the operator rules otherwise.
- Emptying a locked region (`startEmptied` / `endEmptied` in `Wrapper.mjs`) and runtime `column.locked` mutation splitting a group (tracked in `#20511` under `#20379`).
- Column resize on `flex` columns and mid-drag `GroupRow#project()` during resize (tracked in `#20512` / PR `#20514` under `#20379`).

## Avoided Traps

- **Only testing boundary leaves (`Mar` → `May`, `Apr` → `Jan`, `Jan` → `Region`):** a leaf already at the edge of its group has `0` in-group swaps before hitting the boundary, hiding the `currentIndex` mutation on every non-boundary leaf.
- **Allowing an ungrouped column to stop mid-group:** when an ungrouped column crosses a group, it must jump the full group span so the group's leaves never split into two runs.

- 2026-11-07T12:17:59Z @tobiu referenced in commit `9347902` - "feat(grid): a header drag keeps every header group in one piece (#20510) (#20520)

A grouped header whose pointer leaves its group parks the reorder: it
walks back to its own slot while the pointer is outside, and a release
there restores the group's order, however far it travelled inside the
group first. An ungrouped header passes a whole group in one switch,
after travelling the group's full extent, so it can be reordered past a
group without splitting it.

The reorder park moves from the dock's TabSortZone into
container.SortZone#setReorderParked, so both zones share one walk-back.
container.SortZone#getSwitchExtent is the travel threshold hook the grid
header zone widens to a group's run. The over-drag loop ends when
switchItems refuses a step instead of re-polling it every frame."
